\par\smallskip\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\footnotesize Notes: for each inventory, the difference $\ln E^{7\mathrm{th}}-\ln E^{2021}$ is split exactly into a retained-sector term (log change of the sectors reported in both releases) and a scope term (the remainder, from sectors reported in only one release), as in Proposition~3 with releases in place of inventory years. Waste is the only removed sector in 988 of the 1,104 inventories that lose a sector; manufacturing (81) and residential (27) are the most common single additions among the 156 that gain one. Among energy sectors reported in both releases, 61.6\% of inventories have identical values and 12.8\% differ by more than 0.10 ln points; of the 890 inventories with waste in both releases, 77.4\% have a 7th-release value 0.885 times the 2021 value. Variance of the difference: scope term 0.0199, retained-sector term 0.0331, twice their covariance 0.0024. Largest single-inventory share of the pooled residual third moment: 42\% in the 2021 dataset (Table~S23), 170\% in the 7th release before the per-capita screen and 10\% after it.\end{minipage}
